----------------

🎥 Video
===================

Microsoft introduced a reimagined Copilot with three core capabilities: Home, Code, and Autopilot. The announcement also includes Office in Copilot, embedding full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint functionality directly into the Copilot experience.

🔹 Home

Home serves as the new starting point where Chat and Cowork converge. Chat handles instant, conversational interactions: quick questions, lookups, drafts. Cowork handles delegated work that runs end-to-end and returns completed results: RFP responses, launch kits, customer briefings, financial close packages. Microsoft indicated that eventually, users won't need to manually choose a mode. Copilot will route work to the appropriate capability based on the stated intent.

🔹 Code

Code moves solution-building beyond developers. Users describe an app, tracker, dashboard, automation, or workflow in natural language, and Copilot selects an approach and builds it. This is powered by the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot. Microsoft frames this as a fourth unit of knowledge work alongside documents, spreadsheets, and decks: small, purpose-built solutions.

🔹 Autopilot

Autopilot is described as a persistent, proactive, and personal agent that continues working even when the user is not actively engaged. It is expanding to private preview at the end of the month.

🔹 Office in Copilot

The full power of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint is now built into Copilot. Users can ask Copilot to draft a launch brief, model a budget, or build a deck, and it creates or updates a real, editable document. Changes stay in sync between Copilot and Office apps. PowerPoint now keeps decks on-brand automatically and supports fine-tuning of slides and images. Excel shows what changed and why when Copilot or collaborators make edits, and recommends the best chart for data visualization.

🔹 Skills

Skills bring specialized expertise into Microsoft 365 apps: financial skills in Excel, legal skills in Word. Organizations can scale best practices through reusable, role-specific workflows.

🔹 FinOps for AI

New FinOps for AI capabilities were introduced to help organizations manage spend and extract value from Copilot and agents.

🔹 Availability

Home and Code start rolling out in the Frontier program in the coming weeks. Autopilot expands to private preview at the end of the month. Performance and stability in production environments are not independently verified.
